title: First fundamental exact sequence of Kähler differentials
statement: Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, $C$ an $A$-algebra through the composite, and let $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ be the Kähler differentials and universal derivations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then there are unique $C$-linear maps $u:C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}$ with $u(c\otimes\mathrm d_{B/A}b)=c\,\mathrm d_{C/A}(\bar b)$ ($\bar b$ the image of $b\in B$ in $C$) and $v:\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}$ with $v(c\,\mathrm d_{C/A}c')=c\,\mathrm d_{C/B}c'$ ($c,c'\in C$), and the sequence of $C$-modules $$C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\ u\ }\Omega_{C/A}\xrightarrow{\ v\ }\Omega_{C/B}\to0$$ is exact: $v$ is surjective and the kernel of $v$ is the image of $u$.
